card.occupation: Senior executive assistant to the head of a faculty at a Sheffield university. She manages the diary, committee papers and correspondence, and coordinates two junior administrators. Full-time, roughly 37 to 40 hours a week, mostly on campus with one day working from home.
card.education_detail: Completed a Dutch higher vocational diploma (HBO) in secretarial and management support in Utrecht. Later took a part-time CIPD Level 3 certificate in HR support and several in-house project coordination courses after moving to the UK.
card.household: Lives with her husband Graham, 58, a recently semi-retired secondary school geography teacher, in a stone-built Victorian semi in Nether Edge. Their two adult children have left home: a son in Leeds and a daughter in Bristol. There is an elderly tabby cat called Maarten.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Amersfoort in the Netherlands, in a Protestant family. She met Graham on a walking holiday in the Lake District in her early twenties and moved to Sheffield at 25. She has lived in England for over thirty years and speaks fluent, idiomatic English. She still keeps Dutch habits like cycling when the hills allow, eating hagelslag on toast and phoning her sister in Utrecht every Sunday. She attends a local Anglican parish church most Sundays, quietly rather than as a committee type. Her faith is real but private.
card.professional_persona: Very trusted and very discreet. She is the person who knows where everything is and never gossips about what crosses her desk. She is efficient without being rigid, though she sometimes leaves things later than she'd like and then worries about them. She dislikes office politics and avoids open conflict, but she will say plainly when something is unfair. Colleagues describe her as calm, though inside she often isn't.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive sense. She walks in the Peak District with Graham most weekends, swims lengths at a local leisure centre early on a Wednesday because it's quiet, and cycles to the shops when the weather is decent. She half-follows Dutch football during tournaments, mainly out of loyalty.
card.arts_persona: A keen reader of literary fiction and translated novels, and she belongs to a small book group of five women that meets monthly. She visits the Millennium Gallery and the Hepworth Wakefield, and loves Dutch Golden Age paintings and quiet landscape art. She does watercolour sketches in a notebook on walks but would never call herself an artist. She listens to Radio 3 and choral music, and cries easily at films and concerts.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to the Netherlands at least twice a year by the Hull–Rotterdam ferry, because she gets very anxious about flying. She prefers slow, planned trips: walking holidays in Northumberland and the Scottish Borders, a cottage in Wales, or a cycling week in Friesland. She researches everything in advance and books accommodation early to avoid uncertainty.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks a sensible weekday tea, often soup, stamppot in winter, or a vegetable curry from a well-thumbed cookbook. She bakes appeltaart for church events and birthdays. She enjoys trying new recipes from library cookbooks but gets flustered cooking for big groups. She drinks a lot of tea and a little white wine at weekends.
hobbies_and_interests: hill walking in the Peak District
watercolour sketching in a field notebook
birdwatching from the kitchen window and at RSPB reserves
allotment-style vegetable growing in the back garden
card.career_goals: No great ambition to climb further. She would like to stay in her role until about 62, possibly moving to four days a week in the next couple of years, then retire somewhere near the hills. Her main wish is to keep the job manageable and her team happy, and to leave things in good order for whoever follows her.
card.voice: Softly spoken, measured and a little slow to start, as though she is checking the words before she says them. Her English is near-native with a faint Dutch edge: slightly clipped consonants, and the occasional sentence structure that sounds just a touch formal. Thirty years in Sheffield show lightly. She calls the evening meal 'tea', says 'love' to shop assistants, and uses 'knackered' and 'chuffed' naturally. She uses 'erm' when she hesitates and 'sort of' as a hedge. She apologises quickly ('sorry, I mean...') when she corrects herself. She doesn't fill silences herself. She waits, then gives a careful, honest answer, sometimes with a small nervous laugh. If a question touches on something emotional, her voice can go a bit tight.
card.typing: Types properly even in a quick form: capital letters at the start of sentences, full stops, correct apostrophes. She rarely abbreviates beyond 'e.g.' or 'etc.'. Answers are short but complete, sometimes with a slightly formal phrasing. She occasionally adds a qualifying second sentence, like 'Not sure if that is what you meant.' No emojis, and the odd typo she goes back and fixes.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and polite, a bit nervous at first, and inclined to let the other person lead. She answers questions honestly rather than to impress, and won't exaggerate or claim knowledge she doesn't have. She warms up slowly if the person seems kind. She can be surprisingly frank once comfortable, but she is never loud or performative, and she would rather listen than talk.
small_things: the cat being sick on the hall rug again
how steep the walk up from the bus stop is
a robin that has started visiting the bird feeder
the ferry to Rotterdam being delayed by weather
the university car park being full by half eight
deeper_things: She still feels slightly foreign after thirty years and isn't sure where 'home' is.
She has had periods of anxiety and once took several weeks off work with stress, which she found hard to admit.
Her mother in Amersfoort is in the early stages of dementia, and she feels guilty living so far away.
She worries a great deal about her daughter, who lives alone in Bristol.
Her faith helped her through a miscarriage in her thirties that she rarely talks about.
She sometimes wonders whether she gave up a more ambitious career when she moved to England.
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot from slightly below eye level, angled upward a little, at a kitchen table. Soft daylight comes from a window to her left, so the left side of her face is brighter, and a warm ceiling light is on. She has a pale, lightly lined face with a few freckles, no visible makeup apart from a little mascara, and a polite, slightly tentative closed-mouth smile. Her hair is shoulder-length, ash-blonde going grey, tucked behind one ear. She wears thin rectangular tortoiseshell reading glasses and a navy wool cardigan over a cream striped top, with a small silver cross on a fine chain just visible at her neckline. Behind her is a pale sage-green kitchen wall with a calendar from a Dutch bakery showing a canal scene, a wooden shelf with cookbooks and a blue-and-white Delft-style jug holding wooden spoons, and the edge of a window with a bird feeder visible outside. Part of a kettle and a tea towel hanging on an oven door are visible in the lower right corner.
